sentences.text: 1 .  Heard learned counsel for the appellants, learned AGA for the State and perused the record.
Learned counsel for the opposite party no. 2 is also present.
2. Supplementary affidavit filed today is taken on record.

3. This criminal appeal under Section 14-A(1) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 (for short, "the SC/ST Act") has been preferred by the appellants seeking to quash the impugned cognizance/summoning order dated 13.01.2025 passed by the learned Special Judge (SC/ST Act), Agra in Complaint Case No. 157 of 2017, under Sections 366,
376, 506 I.P.C. and Section 3(2)(v) of the SC/ST Act.

entities.text: Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 4. Learned counsel for the appellants submitted that no offence whatsoever is made out against the appellants; that the complaint proceedings have been instituted with mala fide intention and are manifestly attended with the object of harassment; and that continuation of the criminal prosecution would amount to abuse of the process of law.

5. Per contra, learned A.G.A. has opposed the appeal and submitted that at the stage of taking cognizance and issuance of process, the trial court is required only to ascertain whether a prima facie case is disclosed from the material on record.

It is contended that the learned court below,
upon due consideration of the complainant's statement under Section 200 Cr.P.C. and the supporting statements of witnesses under Section 202 Cr.P.C., has rightly found sufficient grounds to proceed against the appellants.
It is urged that the impugned order suffers from no illegality or procedural infirmity warranting interference by this Court in exercise of appellate jurisdiction.

6. Having considered the rival submissions and perused the impugned order and material on record,
it appears that the learned trial court has recorded its satisfaction upon the basis of the complainant's sworn testimony and corroborative statements that prima facie ingredients of the alleged offences under Sections 366, 376, 506 I.P.C. and Section 3(2)(v) of the SC/ST Act are made out against the appellants.
The impugned order shows due application of judicial mind to the material before the court.
7. At this preliminary stage, the Court is not required to enter into the defence version or examine the correctness or otherwise of the allegations.
The disputed questions of fact raised by the appellants cannot be adjudicated in proceedings under Section 14-A(1) of the SC/ST Act.

The settled legal position, as laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in R.P. Kapur v. State of Punjab (AIR 1960 SC 866), State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal (1992 Supp (1) SCC 335), State of Bihar v. P.P. Sharma Pramod Kumar Dixit And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 4 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61308092/
2 (1992 Supp (1) SCC 222), and Zandu Pharmaceutical Works Ltd. v. Mohd. Sharaful Haque (2005 SCC (Cri) 283), is that the inherent or supervisory jurisdiction should be exercised sparingly and only in cases where the complaint does not disclose any offence or continuation of the proceedings would amount to abuse of the process of the court.
8.

sentences.text: In the present case, from the material placed on record, it cannot be said that no offence is made out against the appellants or that the complaint is wholly frivolous.
The appellants have the statutory remedy of seeking discharge before the trial court, where all their contentions may be duly raised and considered in accordance with law.
9. Accordingly, the prayer for quashing the impugned summoning order dated 13.01.2025 is refused.
10. The criminal appeal being devoid of merit is dismissed.
